calls.reason: Acher's May 2025 tests found nearly 9 in 10 o3/o4-mini games ended on an illegal move, with a median game of about 15 moves, so illegal moves by the midgame recur. Quality decline wasn't separately measured.
Anthropic's system card shows jailbreaks still sometimes work but says nothing about cause; its interpretability work points to a different mechanism in an older model. The causal claim is untested.
The LLM+P study adds a formal representation and a classical planner together, so it can't isolate missing world models as the cause. No controlled evidence settles the causal claim.
The 2023 ChatGPT chess study and the 2022 AAAI study describe weaknesses but don't isolate a missing board model as the cause; the former even says ChatGPT can internalise rules.
No study estimates what share of LLM failures comes from lacking explicit world models; the planning and Rubik's Cube studies are narrow and change several factors at once.
The organiser's LinkedIn post reports ChatGPT conceding to Atari Chess (emulated), and Tom's Hardware dates the game to just before June 9, 2025, shortly before the post.
